artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_uses_existing_uv_installs_requested_version_and_verifies_maid
artifacts.source_scenario: A macOS or Linux user already has uv and requests a reproducible MAID Runner version.

expected.behavior: The installer keeps the existing uv, installs the requested maid-runner version with Python 3.12, refreshes tool PATH, and verifies maid --version before succeeding.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_bootstraps_uv_when_missing
artifacts.source_scenario: A macOS or Linux user runs the installer on a machine where uv is absent.

expected.behavior: The installer retrieves Astral's official uv installer, discovers the newly installed uv without restarting the shell, installs MAID Runner, and verifies the command.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_rejects_unsafe_or_incomplete_arguments
artifacts.source_scenario: A caller supplies an unsafe version value, omits the value, or uses an unsupported option.

expected.behavior: The installer exits nonzero with usage guidance before invoking uv for every invalid argument form.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_propagates_download_and_tool_failures
artifacts.source_scenario: The uv download or MAID Runner tool installation fails during bootstrap.

expected.behavior: The installer exits nonzero, does not run maid verification after the failed step, and never prints a success message.

artifacts.name: test_powershell_installer_contract_is_auditable_and_fail_closed
artifacts.source_scenario: A reviewer inspects the Windows bootstrapper in an environment without PowerShell execution support.

expected.behavior: The script validates its version, uses only Astral's HTTPS installer when uv is absent, checks native command exits, installs with Python 3.12, refreshes PATH, and verifies maid before success.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_passes_shellcheck
artifacts.source_scenario: A maintainer validates the published POSIX bootstrapper before deployment.

expected.behavior: ShellCheck accepts the installer with no diagnostics.

artifacts.name: test_readme_and_landing_page_publish_bootstrap_installers_as_primary
artifacts.source_scenario: A newcomer scans the README or landing page for the shortest supported installation path.

expected.behavior: Both surfaces show the maidrunner.dev shell and PowerShell commands before uv and pip alternatives, include the first-run commands, and keep versioned installation concise in the README.

artifacts.name: test_installer_smoke_workflow_runs_local_scripts_on_all_supported_platforms
artifacts.source_scenario: An installer or installer-workflow change is proposed or lands on main.

expected.behavior: A path-scoped workflow executes the checked-out shell installer on Ubuntu and macOS and the checked-out PowerShell installer on Windows with least-privilege contents access.

scope.reason: Public POSIX bootstrap endpoint for macOS and Linux; behavior is exercised as a process by dedicated tests and linted with ShellCheck.
Public PowerShell bootstrap endpoint for Windows; behavior and failure guards are pinned by a source contract because PowerShell is unavailable in the Linux development environment.
The landing-page quick start must make the two first-party bootstrap commands primary and keep direct package commands secondary.
The repository onboarding hierarchy must concisely present the bootstrap installers, version pinning, and advanced uv/pip alternatives.
A path-scoped smoke workflow must execute the local shell and PowerShell installers on Linux, macOS, and Windows runners before they are published.
